messages:
Rina (AE): Customer NexusHealth wants a Private deployment POC. They insist on IP-based allowlists and asked whether we should recommend PrivateLink or a peered topology. Also need firewall snippet and a 2-week estimate for ~100GB.

Marco (NetEng): Short: if they require stable source IPs for allowlisting, peering + customer-controlled NAT with static EIPs is the cleanest. PrivateLink is faster but ENI IPs are ephemeral unless they accept a snapshot for the POC.

Keiko (Solutions): Recommend PrivateLink as default POC (fast), but note the fallback path: peering -> TGW -> NAT with static EIPs for production allowlists.

Anil (Security): We can support mTLS and cert rotation. For the questionnaire: say we support PrivateLink and peering; TLS enforced; mutual TLS available upon request. Provide ephemeral ENI IP list for POC but recommend static EIP for long-term.

Marco (NetEng): Minimal firewall rules for customer (copyable):
```
# PrivateLink flow (POC)
allow tcp from <app-subnet-cidr> to <vpce-enis> port 443
allow udp from <app-subnet-cidr> to <dns-server> port 53
allow udp from <app-subnet-cidr> to 0.0.0.0/0 port 123
# Peering + NAT with static EIP (long-term)
allow tcp from <app-subnet-cidr> to <static-egress-eip> port 443
```
Notes: Use SGs on the interface endpoints instead of hard-coded IP lists where possible.

Keiko (Solutions): Cost estimate (2-week, ~100GB): AWS endpoint/data processing ~$1-5, endpoint hours <$50, Redwood POC support $1k-$2.5k. Peering + NAT adds NAT/EIP hourly charges.

TicketBot: Created ticket POC-5543 for NexusHealth. Connectivity validation window scheduled Thu 11:00-11:30. Assigned Marco.

Marco (NetEng): I'll DM the service name and account IDs and provide an ENI snapshot for the POC window. If they pick peering, ask their netops for a change window and CIDR ranges.

Rina (AE): Great, will send both options and the firewall snippet to NexusHealth. I'll propose PrivateLink first and call out the timeline impact if they want static EIPs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
